short: STFM and the convolutional encoder-decoder (M06) are standard: layout-keeping reduction predates it, baselines are weakened; LRW SOTA claim fails; LM use never stated (M07).
position: The paper [@zhang2019convseq2seq] changes M06 twice: STFM replaces global average pooling before the sequence model, and a convolutional encoder-decoder with width-restricted self-attention replaces the Transformer. Both are standard. Keeping the spatial layout was not new: 7 of 13 prior lip readers that state their reduction use a fully connected layer over the map, two replacing average pooling for the same reason [@stafylakis2017embeddings] [@stafylakis2018pushing] (Appendix), and STFM is tested only against average pooling. The encoder-decoder gains are measured against Transformer baselines the authors call inconsistent with the originals (§4.2); the final 51.7% and 60.1% WER on LRS2 and LRS3 trail TM-seq2seq's LM-free 49.8% and 59.9% [@afouras2018deep]. The state-of-the-art claim (§5) holds on GRID but fails on LRW against an earlier 15.67% error [@stafylakis2018pushing], and the paper does not state the LM condition of its own rows (§3.5, M07).
